step: 0 qualify the readouts (once, before any arm)
question: Can the three readouts and the site be read at all in the preparation?
arms: one plate: untreated; an ISR inducer (thapsigargin or tunicamycin) as positive stress; ISRIB in a concentration series
readouts: phospho-eIF2alpha (Ser51) and total; puromycin or HPG translation labelling; eIF2B assembly shift by sedimentation; phospho-epsilon with total epsilon, only after the antibody has a phosphatase lane and a mutant lane
controls_already_qualified_in_module: positive stress arm and ISRIB reporter potency (EI03, EI04); sedimentation as engagement (EI08, EI16); ATF4 is not an engagement readout in rat cortical cultures (EI22)
decision_it_changes: whether any later arm can be read
if_result_X_then: if the phospho-epsilon antibody fails validation then the GSK3-site level stays unmeasured and step 2 uses translation and the mutants only; no antibody is chosen from the S539 name

step: 1 first fork: is the phospho-eIF2alpha route engaged and limiting
question: Is phospho-eIF2alpha raised and ISRIB-reversible in WWOX-deficient cells against their isogenic corrected cells?
arms: WWOX-deficient and corrected cells, same stage, side by side: untreated; ISRIB concentration series; the positive stress arm
controls_already_qualified_in_module: as step 0; Torin-1 or rapamycin arm separates an mTOR-type block (EI05, E19)
decision_it_changes: prioritises the ISR need against the GSK3 chain; the existing ISR modulator card stays a class card
if_result_X_then: (a) phospho-eIF2alpha raised and ISRIB restores translation: ISR-P route in this preparation, go to step 4 for function, GSK3 branch deprioritised but not refuted; (b) phospho-eIF2alpha not raised and translation lowered: go to step 2; (c) translation not lowered: stop, change stage or cell type before concluding (E18); (d) engagement control fails: uninformative, repeat step 0

question: Do GSK3 inhibitors raise translation in the deficient cells more than in corrected cells, and does the epsilon GSK3 serine move with them?
arms: deficient and corrected cells: vehicle; lithium as the labelled non-specific comparator (G01 card); one ATP-site GSK3 inhibitor; a second of another chemotype; GSK3B versus GSK3A knock-down (H2)
readouts: phospho-epsilon at the GSK3 serine and at the priming serine; translation; phospho-Ser9 of GSK3beta only as a proxy; phospho-S6 kinase and 4E-BP1 as mTOR branch markers
controls_already_qualified_in_module: Gsk3b not Gsk3a lowers phospho-Ser535 in retinal neurons (E13, E14); lithium card G01 as comparator; second chemotype is NOT qualified in the module (H1 names candidates, Ser535 dephosphorylation undocumented for them)
decision_it_changes: whether the GSK3-eIF2B epsilon chain is worth the genetic step; whether lithium-class hypotheses carry beyond non-specific effects
if_result_X_then: phospho-site and translation both move with two chemotypes: go to step 3; translation moves, the site does not: GSK3-other or CMPD (G08), go to step 3b; the site moves, translation does not: not sufficient (G09)

condition_on: step 2 shows translation moves with GSK3 inhibitors
question: Does the effect pass through epsilon?
arms: deficient cells expressing wild-type epsilon, phospho-resistant epsilon (species numbering checked: human 540, mouse 536, rat 535), catalytically dead epsilon (E572A); each with and without the GSK3 inhibitor
readouts: translation; phospho-epsilon (validated) ; expression level of the construct
controls_already_qualified_in_module: S535A raises and E572A removes the translation gain in retinal neurons (E15, E16); Woo 2012 used a double Ser-to-Ala at the GSK and DYRK serines (EN07)
decision_it_changes: whether GSK3-eps or GSK3-other is the contributor
if_result_X_then: no further gain from the inhibitor in the phospho-resistant cells and loss in the dead form: node carries it; the inhibitor still gains in the mutant cells: GSK3-other; a phospho-mimetic is run only to ask whether that form is hypo-active and is not assumed to reproduce phosphorylation (the Ser-to-Asp form in Woo 2012 did not restore the effect); DYRK2 is annotated at the priming serine, so Ala at the GSK3 serine does not separate GSK3 from DYRK2 alone

step: 3b alternative explanations of a translation change
condition_on: step 2 outcome translation moves and the site does not
question: Which other pathway moves translation in the same wells?
arms: vehicle; rapamycin or Torin-1; GSK3 inhibitor with and without
controls_already_qualified_in_module: rapamycin did not remove the S535A regeneration effect (E19); ISRIB does not reverse Torin-1 (EI05)
decision_it_changes: whether the compound effect is attributed to GSK3-eIF2B at all
if_result_X_then: mTOR-branch readouts move with the inhibitor and the Torin arm abolishes the gain: GSK3-other through the mTOR branch; neither: CMPD or an unnamed substrate

condition_on: a translation difference was established in step 1 or 2
question: Does correcting the translation difference change a functional or viability endpoint?
arms: the arm that corrected translation in step 1 to 3, the corrected cells and an untreated deficient arm
readouts: a viability readout and one morphology or network endpoint chosen in advance; no endpoint is chosen after seeing the data
controls_already_qualified_in_module: survival was not improved by removing the GSK3 site (E17); ISRIB raised survival in one ALS-protein model but not another (EI21, EI23)
decision_it_changes: whether the node is a lever for benefit or only a pharmacodynamic marker
if_result_X_then: benefit seen: report as the result of that arm in that cell stage only; no benefit despite translation correction: translation is not the limiting lesion for that endpoint
